newsitem.title: USA: Coram, Integrated Health revise merger terms.
newsitem.headline: Coram, Integrated Health revise merger terms.

text.p: Coram Healthcare Corp, which agreed to be bought by Integrated Health Services Inc in October, said its merger terms with Coram had been revised.
It said the merger deal's previously announced exchange ratio was lowered to 0.15 share of Integrated Health common stock for each share of Coram common stock, from 0.2111 share.

In a separate announcement, Integrated Health said that based on the closing price of its common stock on the last business day prior to the execution of the amendment agreement, it is paying $4.35 per share of Coram common stock in the merger deal.

Integrated Health said it expects to issue 7.11 million shares in the merger and reserve about 2.35 million shares to be issued upon the exercise of outstanding Coram options and warrants. The merger is still intended to qualify as a pooling of interests for accounting purposes, it said.

When the merger deal was announced in October, Integrated Health said it would buy Coram for $280 million in stock and create one of the largest providers of post-operative and in-home health care companies in the nation.

At the time, Integrated Health said it would pay Coram stockholders $5.50 worth of its stock in return for each Coram share. The total value of the merger then, including assumption of Coram's debt and other financial obligations, was estimated at about $655 million.
In its statement, Integrated Health said the amended merger agreement eliminates most of the original closing conditions.

It said that if the amendment became effective, it would be obligated to pay Coram a $25 million break-up fee if the merger were not consummated by May 31, a date which could be extended by either party by up to 60 days.
The amendment agreement is subject to approval by boards of both companies and may be terminated by either company for any reason brefore the close of business on April 4, it said.
The merger itself is subject to the approval by stockholders of the two companies.
